probe_dims: one screen using useOsdkObjects, one using useOsdkFunction, one using useOsdkAction
result: PROBED, PASS, and the carried claim is CONFIRMED BUT OVERSTATED. Confirmed: 8 of 9 useSyncExternalStore call sites in the shipped ESM build pass exactly two arguments, and renderToString of a useOsdkObjects or useOsdkFunction screen really does throw 'Missing getServerSnapshot' — a captured thrown error, not a code reading. OVERSTATED IN TWO WAYS. (1) useOsdkAction never calls useSyncExternalStore at all; an action-only screen server-renders fine. That is exactly the shape of n.surface's 7 CFR 1b.11(a)(46) determination-recording screen, which is therefore server-renderable today. (2) 'throws for any data-bound screen' is false under Suspense: renderToString emits the fallback plus a switch-to-client marker and does NOT throw, renderToStaticMarkup renders the shell with no throw, and renderToPipeableStream keeps the shell. SSR IS NOT BARRED FOR n.surface — only data content inside a boundary defers to the client, which is the ordinary streaming-SSR posture rather than a limitation to design around. The library already knows how: aip/useChat.js:86 passes three arguments. Grepping for the identifier 'getServerSnapshot' is the WRONG test — that string appears nowhere in the shipped build even at the 3-arg site; count call-site arguments. TRAP: useOsdkObjects calls canonicalizeOptions() synchronously before useSyncExternalStore, so with no provider it throws 'No OsdkProvider found' instead, and a probe testing it without a provider would misreport the limitation as absent. A provider is constructible offline; no enrollment was needed to reach the real error. Two packaging traps: @osdk/react/package.json is not resolvable by specifier (the './*' export pattern rewrites it), and mixing ESM @osdk/react with CJS @osdk/client yields two client copies and an error that looks like an SSR failure. Negative-checked: patching a third argument in turns the probe red.
versions: @osdk/react 2.56.0 (npm latest), @osdk/client 2.56.0; exercised under react 19.2.8 AND 18.3.1 with identical results

probe_dims: one query publishing an optional nullable string parameter documented as omittable
result: PROBED. The binding IS defective, but the register named the wrong type, the wrong package, and the wrong symptom. WRONG LOCUS: NotOptionalParams is a module-local unexported type in @osdk/client (two unrelated declarations ship under that name); the hook reads QueryParameterType from @osdk/client/observable. The real defect is one level below, in OptionalQueryParams = { [K in keyof T]: T[K] extends {nullable:true} ? never : K }[keyof T] — despite its name it collects the REQUIRED keys. The polarity is exactly inverted. SYMPTOM BACKWARDS AT THIS BUILD'S DIMENSION: for a query whose only parameter is an optional nullable string, QueryParameterType distributes over never and the params slot collapses to undefined — so OMITTING the parameter is the only thing that compiles, with no cast, and SUPPLYING it fails with TS2322. The register's 'cannot express an absent optional parameter without a cast' is false here. It is TRUE one fixture over: in the mixed case a nullable param comes out REQUIRED and a non-nullable one comes out OPTIONAL, the straight inversion. The register's locus sentence survives — the mismatch is in the binding, not the function: client(q).executeFunction accepts (), ({}) and ({q}) on the same definition with no cast, because it prefers the generator-emitted signature where the hook reaches for QueryParameterType. METHODOLOGICAL TRAP that nearly produced a false green: @osdk/client ships TWO declaration trees and nodenext picks by the consuming package.json 'type' field; a mutation test against build/types/ while tsc reads build/cjs/*.d.cts confirms whatever you already believed. Both trees agree, but check the one your app loads. Mutation-tested: the one-character polarity fix takes the probe from exit 0 to exit 1.
versions: @osdk/react 2.56.0, @osdk/client 2.56.0, @osdk/api 2.56.0; typescript 7.0.2 and 5.9.3, CJS and ESM resolution, 8 invocations

probe_dims: clean install of the generated SDK after moving one function import forward one minor version
result: PROBED. The register's CONCLUSION survives — import list and invoked version are decoupled — but its MECHANISM is refuted and the reality is worse. REFUTED: the generator does not keep emitting the older version. It is faithful to the manifest it is handed; moving a fixture function 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 moves the emitted literal. Anyone acting on the register's mechanism would hunt staleness in the generated client, which is correct. THE ACTUAL DECOUPLING: the version literal is DECORATIVE BY DEFAULT. applyQuery sends `version: query.isFixedVersion ? query.version : undefined`, and isFixedVersion comes from a generator argument fixedVersionQueryTypes that DEFAULTS TO []. So an ordinary SDK emits version:'1.2.0' into its own source and then sends no version at all, and the server resolves 'the latest published version, which may be a pre-release version' per call. That is not a stale-but-diffable pin; it is no pin, and the invoked version can move between two identical deployments with nothing changing anywhere. CONFIRMED ON THE WIRE against a stub fetch: unpinned issues GET/POST with no version param; pinned carries ?version=1.2.0. THE 'SILENTLY' HALF HOLDS: four generations including a version move emitted zero diagnostics through console OR consola (the package's real channel); a server reporting '9.9.9-DISAGREES-WITH-GENERATED' against a client literal of 1.2.0 produced no error and a successful call — applyQuery never compares them. THE PINNING RULE, executed against the shipped @osdk/foundry-sdk-generator: a function is pinned IF AND ONLY IF its import-list entry carries an explicit `:version` suffix, and the external-packages branch returns [] unconditionally so those are ALWAYS unpinned. fixedVersionQueryTypes membership is a bare Array.includes on fullApiName with no validation, so a namespace-qualified or misspelled entry silently unpins the function it was meant to pin. CONSEQUENCE: n.surface/c1's method as written was insufficient and has been tightened. PENDING, genuinely enrollment-blocked: whether a real Developer Console regeneration feeds the generator a manifest carrying the new version (E1).
versions: @osdk/generator 2.56.0, @osdk/client 2.56.0, @osdk/foundry-sdk-generator 2.56.0; generator run offline against a fixture manifest, deterministic across processes

probe_dims: one list of 6 required elements, each with a constrained select, a one-line justification field and 2 evidence links
result: PROBED. BUY REJECTED — G022's hand-built default STANDS, but the register was testing the wrong hinge. The register's disqualifier does not fire: ObjectTable CAN host all three at our 6-element shape. (a) constrained select — EditFieldConfig with fieldComponent 'DROPDOWN' and DropdownEditConfig items/labels/keys; (b) one-line free text — not a named component but the auto-detected default, rendering an <input> (never a textarea, so inherently one-line), with async validateEdit; (c) two evidence links — renderCell returns arbitrary React and a custom locator gives a column with no backing property. THE ACTUAL DISQUALIFIER THE REGISTER NEVER ASKED ABOUT: `objectType` is a REQUIRED prop. ObjectTable is hard-wired to useOsdkObjects/useObjectSet and fetches its own rows from a live ontology. It cannot be handed 6 local rows, and omitting objectType is a hard TS2769. The buy dies on data binding, not cell capability. ESCAPE HATCH the register did not know existed: BaseTable is exported from the same subpath, is generic over any row type, and hosts our exact shape with 6 static local rows, no ontology and no OSDK client — it compiles clean. So 'buy' was never binary; there is a real partial-buy, and it still loses. WHY IT STILL LOSES: the write-back is not included (zero applyAction/createAction references; onSubmitEdits hands you CellEditInfo[] and expects a Promise<boolean>), the select is not constrained by anything typed (items are V[] at V=unknown, so numbers type-check as options for a string property, and nothing reads valueTypeApiName — you hand-maintain the value set either way), and the price measured rather than guessed is 625,822 bytes minified / 198,928 gzipped for one 6-row checklist, buying virtualization, infinite scroll, pinning, resizing and drag-reorder that 6 rows do not need. Only the experimental/object-table subpath exports anything; the package root is a 0-byte index. REVISIT CONDITIONS are written into the probe as assertions: A7 red means objectType became optional, A9 red means the table learned to write back, A8 red means the dropdown became type-bound. PROBE-INFRASTRUCTURE FINDING for every other probe: typescript@7.0.2 is the native port and require('typescript') no longer exposes createProgram, sys or getPreEmitDiagnostics — all three are undefined. Any probe that type-checks must SPAWN the tsc binary.

probe_dims: the v1.2 crosswalk CSV at a pinned commit
result: PROBED, PASS. G007 CONFIRMED: (entity, property) is unique — 292 parsed records, 292 distinct (table, column) pairs, 0 duplicates, no blank keys. The filename was discovered, not guessed: the version lives in the git tag, not the filename. THE OBLIGATION IS 13 ENTITIES — case_event, comment, decision_element, document, engagement, gis_data, gis_data_element, legal_structure, process_decision_payload, process_instance, process_model, project, user_role — derivable only from the CSV, enumerated nowhere in the README. PROVENANCE IS 6 PROPERTIES, present on all 13: data_record_version, data_source_agency, data_source_system, last_updated, record_owner_agency, retrieved_timestamp. TRAP: universal is not provenance. NINE columns appear on all 13 entities — the 6 provenance ones plus id, created_at and other. Deriving the provenance set by asking which columns are universal carries id/created_at/other onto every mapped type as provenance; take the set from the README's explicit enumeration (tie-break rule 7). Header is `table,column,data_type,description,is_generated` and does not use the words entity or property; the mapping comes from the repo README stating it. is_generated is {'NO'} across all 292 rows, so it cannot distinguish stored from computed. wc -l reports 301 against a parsed 292 — descriptions carry embedded newlines. NOT ANSWERED, and refused rather than manufactured: 'how many PIC entities have no counterpart in this build's shape' needs an object-type inventory that does not exist at Phase -1. Recorded as an explicit skip naming the missing operand. Also pinned: the lightweight tag is movable, so the probe now asserts refs/tags/v1.2.0 still equals the commit, via the git-upload-pack refs endpoint.

probe_dims: one SuperRepo via `foundry create`; one object type declared in Ontology-as-code and one imported from the UI; one TypeScript v2 function; one React screen calling it; embedded Ontology preview run locally; one `foundry deploy` to the training enrollment
result: BLOCKED ON THE ENROLLMENT HALF, but the prefab is NOT wholly enrollment-gated and the offline half ran: 54 assertions, 0 failures. THE BIGGEST DE-RISK: the full Ontology-as-code -> IR -> full metadata -> OSDK TypeScript chain runs offline, deterministically, with no token and no network beyond npm. n.ontology can develop and regenerate object types starting now. THE SUPERREPO SHAPE IS KNOWN OFFLINE, read off compiled code and then executed: root marker is foundry.yml; discovery dir .palantir/ holding .<service>-discovery.json; services ontology, typescript-functions, python-functions, platform-api-proxy, plus a status server; the React app's client MUST live at exactly src/client.ts. That reduces G031 to one unknown — what `foundry create` fills into foundry.yml, whose SCHEMA is itself published in @osdk/integration-testing. CONTRADICTS THE REGISTER: the register states on Palantir's roadmap authority that Python functions are NOT supported in SuperRepo, and binds n.drafter on it. The shipped client says otherwise — @osdk/vite-plugin-superrepo carries /local-python-functions as a first-class proxy route, smartClient carries a full PY_RUNTIME with specs/execute endpoints, and a changelog names python-functions as a real service. Either the roadmap is stale or the client is built ahead of a server not yet enabled; this probe CANNOT discriminate offline and the contradiction is recorded rather than resolved from either source. A LIVE VERSION SEAM IN THE G032 FALLBACK: at current public latest-vs-latest, @osdk/vite-plugin-oac 0.55.0 reads irContent.blockData while @osdk/maker 0.54.0 emits `ontology` — the OAC plugin throws at stage 2. It also hardcodes `pnpm exec` and invokes maker on ontology.mts against maker's own ontology.ts default. TWO DECOYS named so they are not re-found: PyPI foundry-cli 0.29.1 is not Palantir's (installs a `pltr` binary), and foundry-dev-tools is the transforms story, not the SuperRepo story. `osdk` CLI has no create and no top-level deploy; it is not a substitute. NOT A SECURITY BOUNDARY: smartClient posts a literal 'Bearer fake-local-dev-token' and the proxy disables TLS verification when a discovery entry has no caCertPath.
blocked_by: G034 — no Foundry enrollment. Stronger than the register assumed: the `foundry` CLI is not on npm or PyPI at all. It is served from each enrollment's own artifacts registry, so Phase -1 on this prefab cannot be delegated to an unenrolled machine or agent.
